sourceMetadata.description: The Mulberry Baptist Association was formed in 1828 by churches in Autauga, Bibb, Dallas, Perry, Shelby and Talladega counties. The Mulberry Association dissolved in 1901.

description: Constituted in 1851 when the Lewis Fork Baptist Association responded in the affirmative to a query by the Little River Church as to whether they might exclude members for joining the Sons of Temperance, a secret society. In reaction, a number of pro-temperance churches withdrew to form this association. In 1857 the Lewis Fork Association rescinded their motion, and the Lewis Fork, Taylorsville, and Lower Creek Associations joined to form the United Baptist Association. (History of North Carolina Baptists Vol. 2 / G. W. Paschal p.315)

The churches in the association (in 1894) were Black River, Bethsaida, Hornett, Mingo, Coharie, Sevn Mile, Reedy Prong, Oak Forest, and Barby's [i.e. Barbry's] Chapel. The composition of church in the association varies slightly over the years. Beginning in 1953 there were some disputes within the association and several churches were dropped over the next few years. These include Black River, Oak Forest and Corinth. They joined together to form their own Seven Mile Primitive Baptist Association
